title: Dated medical events expose household and work pressure on different clocks
source_unit: MEPS 2024 HC-256, HC-036BRR, and HC-254 event files; month-ordered person-level descriptive screens

observations.period: MEPS 2024; first prescription event strictly between R3/1 and R4/2

event_payment.unit: US dollars, weighted mean self/family payment for first event

observations.method: Select the first valid month-ordered prescription event between person-specific R3/1 and R4/2 endpoints, then compare with the complementary round-valid group using PERWT24F and 128 HC-036BRR replicates.
observations.uncertainty: The event may follow a pre-existing need; the comparison group is not event-free; round-level outcomes do not identify the event's claim, fill, bill, remedy, or causal pathway.
observations.subgroup: MEPS respondents with a valid prescription event and round-order fields.
observations.counterinterpretation: The recorded payment is not total price, deductible, balance, unpaid obligation, or forgone-care cost; higher contextual burden need not be caused by the event.

observations.period: MEPS 2024; first emergency-room event strictly between R3/1 and R4/2

event_payment.unit: US dollars, weighted mean self/family payment for first event

observations.method: Month-order the first valid emergency-room event and compare later round-level household and work fields with the complementary round-valid group.
observations.uncertainty: The result is a level comparison with selection, severity, coverage, and endpoint limitations; it does not estimate job loss, event causation, or recovery.
observations.subgroup: MEPS respondents with a valid emergency-room event and round-order fields.
observations.counterinterpretation: An emergency-room event can be downstream of prior illness or household strain, and nonemployment is a status level rather than a transition or earnings loss.

observations.period: MEPS 2024; first inpatient event strictly between R3/1 and R4/2

event_payment.unit: US dollars, weighted mean self/family payment for first event

observations.method: Month-order the first valid inpatient event and compare later round-level household and work fields with the complementary round-valid group.
observations.uncertainty: The inpatient group is selected and small; the screen does not identify admission cause, claim, employment transition, household adaptation, remedy, or recovery.
observations.subgroup: MEPS respondents with a valid inpatient event and round-order fields.
observations.counterinterpretation: The large nonemployment difference may reflect baseline illness, disability, age, or other selection rather than an event-caused work loss.

observations.period: MEPS 2024; prescription event window carried to R5/3

nonemployment_onset.unit: percent versus 7.11% complementary among valid transition cells

nonemployment_resolved.unit: percent versus 5.19% complementary among valid transition cells

observations.method: Carry the prescription event-window definition through valid R5/3 round ordering; use field-specific valid denominators and replicate-weight uncertainty.
observations.uncertainty: The later clock is selected and mixed-direction; transition cells are small; R5/3 is not a verified one-, three-, or six-month recovery endpoint.
observations.subgroup: MEPS respondents with valid three-round prescription-event ordering.
observations.counterinterpretation: Health worsening is not higher in this screen while work-status movement is higher; there is no basis for a single harm or recovery narrative.

denominator.unit: privacy-minimized person/event rows in the staged ledger before event-family screens

event_fields.unit: month-level event dates, payment, care-delay, denial/authorization, and follow-up context are available; claim-level need, alternatives, remedy, meaning/action, and usable geography are not

observations.method: Event-field availability audit over the staged MEPS ledger and the documented dated-event screens.
observations.uncertainty: Availability does not imply valid linkage to an initiating need, claim, provider decision, or household outcome.
observations.counterinterpretation: A same-person event-to-round ordering is stronger than an annual association but remains insufficient for a causal household episode.

related_sources.claim: Dated event-window results and weighting boundaries.
Later health and employment clock comparison.

boundary: This record supports a month-ordered, same-person descriptive event-to-context screen. It does not establish event causation, claim-level need, fill or adherence, payment obligation, alternatives, remedy, household adaptation, verified recovery, trust, political action, switching, or exit. The complementary groups are not causal counterfactuals.
